new.title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras. new.title: Functional and health-related quality-of-life outcomes following stereotactic radiotherapy for glioma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: Functional preservation and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) are increasingly recognized as important treatment outcomes for patients with glioma undergoing stereotactic radiation; however, these outcomes have not been comprehensively synthesized. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating functional and HRQoL outcomes following stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) for glioma. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting standardized functional or HRQoL outcomes following SRS or SRT for newly diagnosed or recurrent glioma were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I v2. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions were performed for binary Karnofsky…

new.title: Sonodynamic therapy for malignant brain tumors: a systematic review​ of preclinical and early clinical evidence.
new.abstract: Glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors are difficult to treat due to the invasive behavior of the disease, resistance to conventional medicines, and the blood-brain barrier that limits delivery of therapeutics. This systematic review evaluates the potential of Sonodynamic Therapy (SDT), a non-invasive therapy that combines low-intensity ultrasound with tumor-selective sonosensitizers to produce fatal reactive oxygen species (ROS). A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Analysis of 36 qualifying studies suggested that SDT could induce tumor-specific apoptosis and necrosis with little injury to healthy brain tissue by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ultrasonic cavitation. new.title: Surgical anatomy of the hypoglossal canal - systematic review with meta-analysis.

Variations in its morphology, particularly bony septations, can complicate skull-base surgeries such as transcondylar or far-lateral approaches. This study aims to provide a meta-analysis of HC prevalence, morphometry, and surgical landmarks. [MATERIALS] A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through December 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Pooled prevalence and mean dimensions were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses explored the impact of sex, side, nationality, and study type. new.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical applications in diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical decision-making.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Epilepsy affects approximately 50 million people worldwide, with disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries where access to specialized care remains limited. Despite advances in neuroimaging and electrophysiology, accurate diagnosis, etiological classification, and timely identification of surgical candidates remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to integrate multimodal data and support clinical decision-making across the epilepsy care continuum. [OBJECTIVE] To systematically assess and meta-analytically quantify the evidence on AI applications for diagnosis, etiological classification, outcome prediction, surgical candidate selection, and workflow optimization in epilepsy. Etiologies were grouped into biologically informed categories (GATORopathies, vascular, overgrowth, copy number variants (CNVs), channelopathies, synaptopathies, and other). new.title: Predictive radiographic risk factors for adjacent segment degeneration following degenerative lumbar spine fusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: To evaluate associations and predictive performance of patient-related, operative, radiographic, and imaging-derived factors for adjacent segment disease (ASD) following degenerative lumbar fusion. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched (January 2026). Observational studies reporting extractable comparative ASD data were included. new.title: Brain-computer interfaces in clinical translation: technological advances, clinical practice and future challenges.
new.abstract: As a transformative technology in neuroengineering, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) establish a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices, independent of peripheral neuromuscular circuits by decoding neural activity and enabling bidirectional feedback. This capability fundamentally reshapes the paradigm of human-machine interaction. Based on the integration depth of neural interfaces, BCIs can be classified into invasive, semi-invasive, and non-invasive approaches, each supporting a range of applications from motor control to cognitive monitoring through multiple paradigms. new.abstract: Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. new.title: Silencing MSR1 in Macrophages Attenuates the Cochlear Foreign Body Response and Preserves Electrode-Neural Interface.
new.abstract: Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Macrophages play a key role in FBR, but their functions are multiple and stage-dependent, and indiscriminate intervention may aggravate cochlear injury. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. new.title: NPD-RSVP: A novel BCI paradigm and decoding method for target recognition.
new.abstract: Rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) can detect and recognize target and non-target objects. In this study, we proposed a novel dual-RSVP paradigm known as negative photographic dual-RSVP (NPD), in which one sequence contains the original target images and the other comprises the corresponding negative photographic images. Compared to the conventional RSVP, the proposed method can provide complementary information about target-related brain signals and efficiently avoid repetition blindness (RB). new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] Deep learning models have been widely applied to predict major depressive disorder (MDD) using magnetoencephalography (MEG) signals. However, these models often suffer from limited performance and generalization. This is primarily due to the strong individual heterogeneity inherent in MEG temporal signals, which makes it difficult for models trained on small samples to distinguish disease-related features and individual-specific features. new.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram.
new.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical, deterministic feature extraction, so that only the classifier was Bayesian. new.title: Artificial Intelligence for Auditory Electrophysiological Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease and Hearing Loss: A Critical Narrative Review.
new.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with a long preclinical phase, making early biomarker discovery essential for timely diagnosis, risk stratification, and intervention. Hearing loss has increasingly been recognized as a clinically important and potentially modifiable factor associated with cognitive decline and dementia risk. Beyond peripheral auditory impairment, accumulating evidence suggests that central auditory dysfunction, altered auditory processing, and electrophysiological abnormalities may emerge during the course of AD and related cognitive disorders. new.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. new.abstract: BACKGROUND This study compared a rehabilitation program using Luna EMG biofeedback with conventional physiotherapy in patients in the chronic phase after stroke, focusing on hand motor function, upper limb proprioception, and functional ability. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 124 post-stroke patients aged 45-75 years were randomly assigned to a test group (n=63) or control group (n=61). Both groups completed a 3-week rehabilitation program. new.title: Postmortem computed tomography findings in drowning: a systematic review of diagnostic usefulness.
new.abstract: [OBJECTIVES] Drowning is a challenging forensic diagnosis, and postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) is increasingly used as an adjunct. This systematic review synthesizes PMCT findings in drowning and evaluates the diagnostic usefulness of individual imaging signs. [MATERIALS AND METHODS] PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through July 2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Original studies reporting PMCT findings in human drowning cases were included. A study-family approach was used to address cohort overlap, and quality was assessed using a modified Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. new.title: Predictive Modeling of Sarcopenia Using Machine Learning: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Sarcopenia is an age-related syndrome characterized by muscle loss and functional decline, increasing fall risks. Early identification is crucial, yet convenient and accurate screening tools remain limited in routine practice. Machine learning (ML) models show promise for early sarcopenia detection, but their diagnostic performance and methodological quality have not been systematically quantified. [OBJECTIVE] This review aimed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic performance of ML models for sarcopenia prediction, compare performance across ML algorithms, and identify key sources of heterogeneity and methodological limitations. new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] This study reviews methods that integrate biomedical knowledge graphs (BKGs) and large language models (LLMs) for clinical applications. Unlike prior surveys that address LLMs or BKGs in isolation, or lack a systematic review methodology, we analyze the literature along two complementary axes-clinical and methodological-for navigating challenges and opportunities at the intersection of artificial intelligence and healthcare. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Medical vision-language models combine images and text to answer questions, generate reports, and support image interpretation. Task accuracy alone does not establish whether their outputs depend on relevant visual evidence or remain reliable under changes in the input. [OBJECTIVE] This study aimed to describe how trustworthiness is evaluated in medical vision-language models, identify gaps in evaluation and reporting, and develop a preliminary minimum evaluation checklist. [METHODS] We conducted a scoping review using the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Emergency departments (EDs) depend on rapid, reliable triage for patient safety and flow. The Manchester Triage System (MTS) is widely implemented but exhibits known interrater variability. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential decision-support tools for triage and early assessment, yet real-world comparative evaluations remain scarce. ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] The safety of omitting up-front treatment with aspirin during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear. ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is increasingly used for revascularization of unprotected left main coronary artery disease. Whether intravascular ultrasonographic (IVUS) guidance during PCI results in better clinical outcomes than conventional angiographic guidance alone is uncertain. ns.title: The Safety and Outcomes of Elective Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in the Elderly: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis.
ns.abstract: [PURPOSE] Prevalence of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) increases with age. Previous trials confirm that elective endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an effective intervention for AAA. However, few elderly patients were recruited into randomized trials, whereas in contemporary clinical practice, elective repair is commonly performed on octogenarians. We evaluated the safety and outcome of elective EVAR in elderly patients to inform clinical practice and vascular service provision. [METHODS] A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting risk of complications and death in patients undergoing elective EVAR was performed (PROSPERO CRD: 42022308423). bmi.abstract: Electroencephalography-based brain-computer interfaces have revolutionized the integration of neural signals with technological systems, offering transformative solutions across neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical practice. This review systematically analyzes advancements in electroencephalography-based brain-computer interface architectures, emphasizing four pillars, namely signal acquisition, paradigm design, decoding algorithms, and diverse applications. The aim is to bridge the gap between technology and application and guide future research. bmi.abstract: Previous research has demonstrated the potential of using pre-trained language models for decoding open vocabulary Electroencephalography (EEG) signals captured through a non-invasive Brain-Computer Interface (BCI). ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Prediabetes is a prevalent condition in which early detection and lifestyle interventions can prevent or delay progression to diabetes. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer enhanced tools for diagnosis, risk stratification, and scalable delivery of lifestyle interventions. This review synthesizes current applications of AI/ML in patients with prediabetes. [METHODS] We conducted a scoping review using PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science (through May 2025) to identify original studies applying AI/ML to prediabetes prediction or management. ai.title: Epicardial and pericardial adipose tissue: anatomy, physiology, imaging, segmentation, and treatment effects.
ai.abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. We sought to discuss the currently used imaging modalities to assess these fat compartments-CT, MRI, and echocardiography-emphasizing their advantages, limitations, and the urgent need for standardization for both scanning and image reconstruction. ai.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent.
ai.abstract: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni's action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. ai.title: A deep learning framework for efficient pathology image analysis.
ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed digital pathology by enabling biomarker prediction from high-resolution whole-slide images. However, current methods are computationally inefficient, processing thousands of redundant tiles per slide and requiring complex aggregation models. We introduce EAGLE (Efficient Approach for Guided Local Examination), a deep learning framework that emulates pathologists by selectively analyzing informative regions. EAGLE combines task-agnostic tile selection with detailed feature extraction and is benchmarked against leading slide- and tile-level foundation models across 43 tasks from nine cancer types spanning morphology, biomarker prediction, treatment response and prognosis. ai.title: Deep learning electrocardiogram model for risk stratification of coronary revascularization need in the emergency department.
ai.abstract: [BACKGROUND AND AIMS] Identification of patients with acute coronary syndrome requiring coronary revascularization can be challenging due to inconclusive electrocardiogram (ECG) findings or biomarker results. A deep learning model to detect ECG patterns associated with revascularization likelihood was developed, aiming to guide further assessment and reduce diagnostic uncertainty. [METHODS] A convolutional neural network model was trained on 144 691 ED visits from a US cohort (60 ± 19 years; 53% female; 0.6% revascularization), tested on a separate test cohort (n = 35 995), and benchmarked against clinician ECG interpretation and cardiac troponin T (TnT). ai.title: Foundation models for radiology: fundamentals, applications, opportunities, challenges, risks, and prospects.
ai.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) represent a significant evolution in artificial intelligence (AI), impacting diverse fields. Within radiology, this evolution offers greater adaptability, multimodal integration, and improved generalizability compared with traditional narrow AI. Utilizing large-scale pre-training and efficient fine-tuning, FMs can support diverse applications, including image interpretation, report generation, integrative diagnostics combining imaging with clinical/laboratory data, and synthetic data creation, holding significant promise for advancements in precision medicine. However, clinical translation of FMs faces several substantial challenges. ai.title: Human versus artificial intelligence: evaluating ChatGPT's performance in conducting published systematic reviews with meta-analysis in chronic pain research.
ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large-language models like Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), has demonstrated potential in streamlining research methodologies. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses, often considered the pinnacle of evidence-based medicine, are inherently time-intensive and demand meticulous planning, rigorous data extraction, thorough analysis, and careful synthesis. Despite promising applications of AI, its utility in conducting systematic reviews with meta-analysis remains unclear. This study evaluated ChatGPT's accuracy in conducting key tasks of a systematic review with meta-analysis.
